content.user_title: Build Rust Services with Guts Patterns
content.value_statement: Rust teams need consistent project patterns for Guts services. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for idiomatic Rust, async design, and commonware integration.
actual_capabilities: Recommends cargo fmt and cargo clippy checks before commits.
Shows thiserror-based library error patterns with typed Result aliases.
Demonstrates Tokio channel patterns for async service requests.
Defines a simple Rust module layout with public API re-exports.
Lists commonware crates for cryptography, p2p, consensus, storage, and codec work.
Provides Cargo.toml conventions for metadata, lints, dependencies, and Rust version.
limitations: Focused on Guts project conventions, not every Rust domain.
Does not include executable scripts or automated project changes.
Commonware examples assume those crates are available in the project.
Does not replace compiler checks, tests, or security review.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Guts Rust module
use_cases.description: Apply shared error handling, module layout, documentation, and lint expectations to a new crate.

use_cases.title: Review async service design
use_cases.description: Check whether a service uses Tokio channels and structured request handling in a maintainable way.

use_cases.title: Prepare commonware integration
use_cases.description: Identify relevant commonware crates and Cargo metadata for decentralized infrastructure components.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Rust Style Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a new Rust file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust module for the Guts style guide. Focus on formatting, documentation, Result types, tests, and clear module boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Help design typed errors for this Guts library crate. Use thiserror-style variants, clear messages, and a public Result alias.

prompt_templates.title: Review Async Service Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this async service design. Check Tokio usage, channel boundaries, request reply flow, ownership, and testability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Commonware Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Guts component that uses commonware primitives. Recommend relevant crates, module structure, Cargo metadata, lints, tests, and performance checks.

output_examples.input: Review this new repository module for Guts conventions.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering public documentation, typed errors, module exports, async boundaries, tests, and required Cargo checks.

output_examples.input: Help design an async service for repository queries.
output_examples.output: A service outline using Tokio channels, request and reply separation, clear error propagation, and focused test cases.

output_examples.input: Prepare Cargo metadata for a Guts crate.
output_examples.output: A checklist for package fields, Rust version, license, workspace dependencies, lint settings, and repository metadata.

best_practices: Run formatting, linting, and tests before asking for final review.
Share the target crate role, public API, and expected commonware dependencies.
Ask for focused feedback on errors, async design, module layout, or Cargo metadata.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to bypass Rust safety checks or justify unnecessary unsafe code.
Do not use the examples as complete production implementations without review.
Do not assume commonware crate choices are correct for every decentralized system.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply Guts Rust conventions for style, errors, async services, commonware crates, testing, and Cargo configuration.

faq.question: Can it write full Rust crates?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and review code, but final implementation still needs compiler checks, tests, and human review.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents common Cargo commands, but the skill itself does not execute commands.

faq.question: Is it specific to the Guts project?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tuned for Guts and commonware-based decentralized infrastructure work.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover security review?
faq.answer: It encourages memory safety and clear patterns, but it is not a complete security audit process.
